summary: A short boot animation shown once per browser session before the first page renders. It draws the logo and prints real figures fetched from the API (the size of the rulebook and the number of stored events) alongside a progress bar; any key press or click skips it, and it is skipped entirely when motion is reduced. main.js awaits `boot()` before routing to the first page.

notes.text: File header: on the first visit of a browser session, a short boot screen reports real numbers from the API while the logo draws itself. Any key press or click skips it, and with reduced motion it is skipped entirely.
Imports `get` to fetch the figures shown during boot.
Imports `$`, `esc` (escapes text for safe use in HTML) and `sleep` (a promise that resolves after a given number of milliseconds).
Imports the motion-aware `animate`, `drawIn` (the SVG line-drawing effect) and `motionEnabled`.
`boot()` is async; main.js awaits it before rendering the first page, so the dashboard appears only after the boot screen has faded.
`#boot` is the overlay defined (hidden) in index.html; `seen` will record whether it already played in this session.

Reads the `iip-booted` flag from `sessionStorage` and then sets it, so the sequence plays once per tab session and reloads skip it. Storage access can throw (for example when site data is blocked); the error is ignored and the boot just plays.

Skips everything when the boot already ran or motion is off (OS reduced-motion setting, the in-app toggle, a hidden tab or anime.js missing). The overlay is removed from the page entirely, not just hidden.
Shows the overlay.
`skipped` turns true as soon as the user asks to skip, and `skip` is the handler that sets it.
Any key press anywhere, or a click on the overlay, calls `skip`. `{ once: true }` makes each listener remove itself after it fires.

Starts fetching the rulebook and the integration health in parallel right away, so the requests overlap the logo animation. If either fails, `.catch` substitutes `[null, null]` and the boot falls back to generic text instead of breaking.
Draws the logo's two `.trace` strokes as if with a pen, 900ms each, the second starting 120ms after the first.
After 600ms the logo's dot (`.core`) pops in from scale 0, using `outBack(3)`, an ease that overshoots a little and settles back.
The title fades in and slides 8px from the left, starting after 300ms.
The progress bar's inner element. CSS starts it at `scaleX(0)`, growing from the left edge.
Waits for the API figures. The logo animations above were started but not awaited, so they keep playing in the meantime.
The boot log lines; the first one is fixed text.
Real numbers from `/risk/rules`: how many signals and risk levels the engine knows (currently 11 signals and 4 levels), or plain text if that call failed.
A real number from `/integration/health`: how many events are stored, with thousands separators from `toLocaleString()`.
A final fixed line; the array closes.
The container the lines are added to.
Loops over the lines with their index, and stops adding lines as soon as the user has skipped.
Appends one line with a check mark. `insertAdjacentHTML` parses HTML, so the text, which contains numbers from the API, is escaped with `esc()` first.
Fades the new line in while sliding it 6px from the left.
Grows the progress bar to the share of lines shown so far, for example 0.5 after two of four.
Pauses 260ms before the next line; then the loop closes.
Unless skipped, holds for another 220ms so the last line can be read.
Removes the keydown listener in case it never fired (`once` only removes it after it fires). The click listener needs no cleanup because its element is removed below.
The exit: the overlay fades out, grows by 1.5% and blurs to 6px over 480ms, and the function waits for that to finish.
Removes the overlay from the page for good and closes `boot()`.
